findings.failure_path: table_data_anchor_valid accepts any added data cell in an owner-scoped changed .md with a header+delimiter. source-register.md is itself such a table under skills/skill-extraction-workflow/references/. An author can add a ledger row and set firing-path: file:skills/skill-extraction-workflow/references/source-register.md#<text unique to that new row>: the anchor is absent from base, present in the round's added lines, unique in file, and sits in a data cell of an explicit table. The row then certifies itself with no changed rule or executable anywhere. No fixture covers a firing path pointing at the ledger file.
findings.smallest_fix: Reject table (and file) firing paths whose path is LEDGER_PATH / the source register itself.

findings.failure_path: Rule 4 previously made a missing cut-list/manual-fallback a blocking `blocked` mark that the user could not waive. Now the agent may itself decide appetite is `not-applicable` "仅做影响范围盘点" or treat a user request as 省略展示, and ship the table with no appetite tradeoff and no blocked marker. The gated refusal is reachable-around by the gated party's own classification, with no independent trigger; eval/body-compliance-eval.rb's new scope-appetite-na probe forbids the blocking wording, so the regression is codified as expected behavior.
findings.smallest_fix: Require the not-applicable/omission branch to record an explicit user-or-human decision reference (as with human-decision in rule 1) rather than an agent-inferred task boundary.

findings.failure_path: On the cancellation path the original BaseException is re-raised inside `except`, then `finally: p.stdin.close()` runs. With buffered unwritten prompt bytes and a dead child, close() flushes and raises BrokenPipeError, which replaces the original KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit/timeout identity that the register row claims is preserved. test_eval_runtime.py substitutes io.StringIO for p.stdin, which never raises on close, so every cleanup test would pass with the bug present.
findings.smallest_fix: Wrap the stdin/stdout closes in try/except (BrokenPipeError, OSError): pass, and add a fake stdin whose close() raises.

findings.failure_path: Novelty is tested only as absence from the same path in base (`blob_at.call(scope.base, parts[:path])`). Moving a definition verbatim from one owner file to another (or renaming the file) makes the anchor absent from the new path's base while the text is unchanged in the round, so a pure relocation buys a RED-baseline firing path. The 14 negative cases test survival within one file only.
findings.smallest_fix: Also reject when the anchor exists anywhere in the owner's base tree, not just at parts[:path].

findings.failure_path: R7's SLI requirement now has an author-declared escape: any cause-based alert can be shipped as an "actionable capacity or impending-failure" alert using raw internal metrics. The added reference text asks for evidence/action/owner but nothing checks them, and the old blocking sentence ("Alerts evaluate against SLIs, not raw metrics") is gone, so the paging-spam rule is now unenforceable prose.
findings.smallest_fix: State that a non-SLI alert must record the forecast/threshold evidence and owner inline with the rule, and that an alert lacking them is not permitted to page (P0).

concern_results.conclusion: Counterexamples found. The new table-anchor path accepts any added data cell in an owner-scoped .md, including source-register.md's own ledger table, so a row's own text can satisfy the firing path it declares; and a definition moved verbatim between files of the same owner passes the base-absence test although no text is new (fixtures only cover same-file survival). Round/owner binding and uniqueness checks are unchanged and do hold. The doc rows for platform-observability, platform-service-connectivity and product-rd-workflow declare RED-baseline/observed-failure: yes on the strength of unexecuted, author-run "source-contract comparisons"; the gate only proves anchor location, exactly as the diff states, so those rows are attribution, not measured outcome. Retry/alerting definitions were substantively corrected (VirtualService retry ownership, budget arithmetic, outlier interval semantics), but R7's new "capacity/impending-failure" branch is self-adjudicated.

Two gated outcomes are reachable without their upstream trigger. requirement-scope hard rule 4 previously blocked an appetite field lacking cut-list/manual fallback even when the user said not to write it; the rewrite lets the agent itself declare `not-applicable` or "omit presentation" from task boundaries, and the new eval probe rewards it — the gated party adjudicates its own exemption. The impact-chain firing-path gate can be satisfied by the declaration surface itself (ledger table row) rather than a changed rule. Evaluator cleanup/uncertainty propagation is otherwise sound, except the `finally: p.stdin.close()` can raise BrokenPipeError and replace the original exception; the tests use StringIO stdin and cannot observe this.

challenge_focus: Challenge evidence attribution and execution boundaries independently: changed-table anchors versus hidden or surviving text, round and owner binding, mandatory evidence declarations, original exceptions and uncertain descendant cleanup, and network retry/alerting definitions. Seek concrete counterexamples beyond the accepted fixture; distinguish source accuracy from location checks and measured model outcomes.
